title: Isolation of autophagic fractions from mouse liver for biochemical analyses
protocol: Place 500 mL of 0.25 M sucrose and PBS on ice.
Fill two 50 mL FalconTM tubes with 50 mL of 0.25 M sucrose each.
Add 500 μL of protease inhibitor cocktail to each FalconTM tube.
Add 500 μL of phosphatase inhibitor cocktail to each FalconTM tube.
Keep the two 50 mL tubes on ice.
Pool three livers into one 50 mL FalconTM tube containing 15 mL of 0.25 M sucrose.
Gently rinse isolated livers in a 50 mL beaker with ice-cold PBS to remove excess blood.
Remove the gallbladder carefully using a razor blade to avoid contamination.
Dice the liver into smaller pieces to facilitate homogenization.
Add fresh 0.25 M sucrose containing protease and phosphatase inhibitors to the diced livers.
Transfer the liver pieces in 0.25 M sucrose to a WHEATON® SAFE-GRIND® Potter-Elvehjem tissue grinder for homogenization.
Filter the liver homogenate through a 4×4 2-ply gauze into a clean FalconTM tube to eliminate lipids floating on top of the homogenate.
Add protease and phosphatase inhibitors (cocktails 2 and 3) to the samples.
Homogenize the liver using a WHEATON® SAFE-GRIND® Potter-Elvehjem tissue grinder with a PTFE pestle tip in a cold room within a temperature range of 4°C–7°C.
Mix the liver samples in 15 mL of 0.25 M sucrose.
Rotate the PTFE pestle tip at maximum speed inside the tube containing the sample.
Perform ten strokes per sample to ensure there are no clumps or residual pieces of liver.
Ensure the tissue grinder remains completely submerged in ice during manual homogenization.
Visually confirm that there are no large pieces of liver remaining after homogenization.
Filter the liver homogenate through a 4×4 2-ply gauze into a clean FalconTM tube.
Place the gauze over the top of the 50 mL FalconTM tube.
Use a clean spatula to create a small dip/cup shape into the gauze.
Pour the homogenate into the gauze for filtration.
Lift the sides of the gauze and use a spatula to secure the sides of the gauze.
Repeat steps a through d until all the liver homogenate has been filtered.
Gently squeeze the gauze with forceps to eliminate any residual homogenate into the tube.
Discard the sequestered fat in the gauze.
Remove 100–150 μL of homogenate for western blotting.
Proceed with the next step using the remaining homogenate for autophagic fractions.
Filter the liver homogenate.
Centrifuge the filtered liver homogenate at 2,000 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Collect the supernatant containing ER, cytosol, autophagic, and lysosomal fractions into a new 50 mL tube on ice.
Fill the 50 mL Falcon tube with the pellet with enough fresh ice-cold 0.25 M sucrose to fill it to 35 mL gently.
Centrifuge the sucrose-filled pellet again at 2,000 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove as much supernatant from the second spin and add it to the original 50 mL tube containing the initial supernatant.
Discard the 50 mL tube with the pellet after removing all possible supernatant.
Spin the 50 mL tube containing the combined supernatant at 12,000 rpm (17,000 g) for 12 minutes at 4°C.
Remove and discard the supernatant without disturbing the autophagic fractions pellet.
Resuspend the autophagic fractions pellet in fresh 0.25 M sucrose to the desired volume.
Spin the 50 mL tube at 12,000 rpm for 12 minutes at 4°C.
Eliminate as much of the supernatant as possible via vacuum suction.
Label four 15 mL tubes as 26%, 24%, 20%, and 15% respectively.
Calculate the total amount of Nycodenz needed per sample according to the provided chart.
Prepare enough Nycodenz for the number of samples being prepared.
For each sample, add 4 ml of 26% Nycodenz.
Add 2 ml of 24%, 20%, and 15% Nycodenz layers respectively.
Resuspend pellet in 950 μL of 0.25 M sucrose containing protease inhibitors.
Add 1.4 mL of 85.6% Nycodenz and mix well.
Pipette the sample into a 13.2 mL Beckman Coulter ultracentrifuge tube without touching the sides.
Slowly add 26% Nycodenz using an extended fine tip transfer pipet.
Add four mL of 26% Nycodenz to each gradient immediately above the existing layer.
Pipette the 24% Nycodenz layer on top of the 26% layer.
Pipette the 20% Nycodenz layer on top of the 24% layer.
Pipette the 15% Nycodenz layer on top of the 20% layer, with the 15% layer at the top.
Add a small amount of 0.25 M sucrose to the top of the layers.
Balance the Beckman Coulter Ti41 buckets using 0.25 M sucrose.
Load the balanced buckets onto the SW41 Ti ultracentrifuge rotor.
Centrifuge the gradients for 3 hours at 104,333 × g at 4°C.
Remove the 13.2 mL tubes from the buckets after centrifugation.
Use a 1 mL transfer pipet to collect the different autophagic fractions.
Gently suction to remove the top layers until reaching the autophagosome fraction.
Suction out the autophagosome fraction into 5 mL Ultra-Clear centrifuge tubes.
Repeat this step to individually collect the autolysosomal and lysosomal fractions in separate tubes.
Add ice-cold 0.25 M sucrose with inhibitors to each tube until 0.5 cm from the top of the tubes.
Spin down the samples at 30,000 × g for 1 hour at 4°C in a TLA-110 rotor on an Ultracentrifuge.
Pellet the fractions at 21,000 × g for 1 hour to maintain the architecture of the autophagic fractions.
